mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt engine for a BMW 528i typically costs £2,500-£6,500 supply-only depending on the generation and engine code. Used units start from £800, reconditioned from £2,125. Fitting adds approximately 8-14 hours of labour at specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW F10 528i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N20 engine in the F10 528i (2010-2016) is prone to timing chain guide failure. Warning signs include a whining or rattling noise from the front of the engine on startup or under acceleration. If you hear this noise, have it inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW E39 528i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The E39 528i is increasingly recognised as an appreciating modern classic. A well-maintained E39 528i is worth £2,000-£6,000. If the car is solid and the replacement cost makes financial sense, many owners choose to invest in a quality rebuild.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 528i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 528i engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop, including removal, fitting, and testing. Supply-only delivery is usually 1-3 working days. Complexity varies by generation.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 528i engines across generations?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 528i badge has covered five different engines: the M30B28 (E12/E28, 184hp, 2.8L straight-six), M52B28 (E39, 190hp), M54B30 (late E39, 231hp), N52B30 (E60, 215-230hp), and N20B20 (F10, 242-245hp, 2.0L turbo four-cylinder).

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 528i replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt or reconditioned BMW 528i engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Some suppliers offer extended coverage on premium rebuilds. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 528i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 528i has been a mainstay of the 5 Series range since 1976, representing the sweet spot between performance and refinement across five generations. From the carburetted M30 straight-six of the E12 through to the turbocharged four-cylinder N20 of the F10, the 528i badge has always stood for accessible straight-six performance - until the downsizing era arrived.

milestones.description: **1976** - E12 528i launched with M30B28 2.8-litre straight-six, carburettor-fed, 184hp
**1979** - E12 facelift introduces Bosch L-Jetronic fuel injection, power rises to 184hp
**1981** - E28 528i replaces E12, carrying over the M30B28 with Motronic fuel injection, 184hp
**1995** - E39 528i launched with M52B28 2.8-litre straight-six, 190hp, aluminium block, double-VANOS
**1996** - M52B28 gains single VANOS on intake cam, 193hp
**1998** - M52TUB28 introduces double-VANOS and drive-by-wire throttle
**2004** - E60 528i (US-only initially) arrives with N52B30 3.0-litre straight-six, 215hp, magnesium-aluminium composite block
**2010** - F10 528i launched with N20B20 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder, 242hp, twin-scroll turbo, Valvetronic

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 5 Series 528i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 2.8L Straight-Six Petrol (1976-1987)
items.commonFailure: The M30's mechanical fuel injection (K-Jetronic on early cars) and ageing wiring looms can cause running issues. Valve stem seals harden with age, leading to oil consumption on startup. Timing chain guides should be inspected.

items.title: 2.8L Straight-Six Petrol (1995-2000)
items.commonFailure: The M52B28's aluminium block is sensitive to overheating - head gasket failure is common if the cooling system is neglected. VANOS seals degrade, causing rough idle and loss of low-end torque. Oil consumption from piston ring wear is also reported.
items.cta: -> Get quotes for M52B28 BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement
items.closing: -> Get quotes for M52B28 BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement

items.title: 3.0L Straight-Six Petrol (2000-2003)
items.commonFailure: The M54B30 shares the M52's VANOS seal degradation issues. DISA valve failure causes power loss. Oil consumption from piston rings is a known issue. Timing chain guides can fail at higher mileages, though the chain itself is generally durable.

items.closing: -> Get quotes for M54B30 BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement

items.title: 3.0L Straight-Six Petrol (2004-2010)
items.commonFailure: The N52's magnesium-aluminium composite block is generally robust. Oil consumption from piston ring design is reported. Valve lifter tick on cold start is common but not catastrophic. Electric water pump failure is a known weak point.
items.cta: -> Get quotes for N52B30 BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement
items.closing: -> Get quotes for N52B30 BMW 5 Series 528i engine replacement

items.title: 2.0L Turbocharged Four-Cylinder Petrol (2010-2016)
items.commonFailure: The N20's timing chain and guide assembly is the primary failure point. Symptoms include a whining or rattling noise from the front of the engine on startup. Chain failure can cause catastrophic engine damage. Other issues include charge pipe cracking and VANOS solenoid failure.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 528i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 528i's engine reliability varies dramatically by generation - earlier M30 and M52 units are generally robust but age brings cooling system and VANOS issues, while the later N20 turbo four suffers from well-documented timing chain failures. Rebuilt 528i engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N20 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series F10 528i Needs Early Warning
problems.rootCause: The N20's timing chain tensioner can fail, allowing the chain to slacken and wear against plastic guides. If the guides break, the chain can jump teeth or snap, causing catastrophic piston-to-valve contact.

repairOptions.longevity: Essential if rattling is heard; cheapest option
When chain has failed or caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical F10 528i (2010-2016) is worth roughly £4,600-£8,900 depending on condition and mileage. If you're facing a full rebuilt engine at £4,800-£6,500 plus fitting, the replacement cost may approach or exceed 60% of a lower-value F10's market value. For well-maintained examples, the maths is more favourable.
problems.recommendation: If your F10 528i's N20 engine makes a whining or rattling noise on startup, have the timing chain inspected immediately - catching it early can save the engine. If the chain has already failed, a rebuilt N20 with upgraded timing components and warranty is the sensible route.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N20B20 BMW 5 Series 528i engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series E39 528i Overheats
problems.rootCause: The M52 and M54's cooling systems use plastic components - water pump impellers, expansion tanks, and radiator end tanks - that become brittle with age and heat cycles. Failure leads to rapid coolant loss and overheating, which can warp or crack the aluminium cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative - recommended every 5 years or 60k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head removal, skim/test, new gasket, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: Only if damage is minor and the block is sound
When head is beyond repair or block damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E39 528i (1996-2003) is worth roughly £2,000-£6,000 depending on condition. The E39 is increasingly recognised as an appreciating modern classic - many owners choose to invest in a quality rebuild rather than scrap a well-preserved example.
problems.recommendation: Preventative cooling system maintenance is cheap relative to the alternatives. Replace the water pump and expansion tank proactively. If your E39 528i has overheated, get the head inspected promptly - catching a minor warp early can save the engine. Given the E39's growing classic status, a quality rebuild often makes more sense than repeated patch-up repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M52B28 / M54B30 BMW 5 Series 528i engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS & DISA Failure - Loss of Power in the BMW 5 Series E39 528i
problems.rootCause: The M52 and M54's VANOS (variable valve timing) system uses rubber seals that degrade with age and heat, causing oil pressure loss and poor camshaft timing adjustment. The DISA valve (variable intake manifold) can fail, causing a loss of low-end torque and a rattling noise.

repairOptions.longevity: If rough idle or loss of low-end power is noticed
If rattling noise from intake or power loss
When multiple issues combine or engine has sustained damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - E39 528i values typically £2,000-£6,000. VANOS and DISA repairs are relatively affordable compared to a full engine replacement and can restore lost performance.
problems.recommendation: VANOS seal degradation is almost inevitable on high-mileage M52 and M54 engines. Replacing the seals with upgraded Viton units is a cost-effective repair that restores low-end torque and smooth idle. Do not ignore the DISA rattle - a failed DISA flap can break apart and be ingested into the engine.
